fixes.explanation: The text says the opposite, friend. The man says, "He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains." (Lamentations 3:7) He's walled in and weighed down, so slipping out isn't on the table. I think that's a heavy spot to be in.

False is right. The man says, "He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains." (Lamentations 3:7) He says he cannot escape, so he's not slipping out whenever he likes. Walls around him and chains weighing him down, and I think that's a heavy spot to be in.

The verse doesn't say his voice gives out. It says, "Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer." (Lamentations 3:8) The problem he names is that his prayer is shut out. That's the part that stings.

That's a different picture. The verse says, "He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush." (Lamentations 3:10) The bear and the lion are waiting and hiding, and there's no mention of young anywhere. Waiting and hiding is the picture the man gives.

Sleeping in a den isn't the verse, friend. The man says, "He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush." (Lamentations 3:10) Those two are hiding and waiting, and sleeping isn't in the picture. I think that's what makes it so frightening.

Land isn't in this verse. The man says, "My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD." (Lamentations 3:18) His strength and his hope are the two things he names. I think that sounds like running on empty.
